nodes.content: Develop a learned surrogate for compressible Euler dynamics that preserves conservation and entropy admissibility across shocks on unseen meshes.
requirements: Keep normalized mass, momentum, and energy drift below 10⁻⁶ over 1,000 periodic, unforced timesteps.
Match an entropy-stable finite-volume baseline’s shock accuracy without increasing discrete entropy violations on unseen meshes.

nodes.content: Learn mesh-equivariant, positive-semidefinite entropy-variable dissipation around entropy-conservative face fluxes, with shared face updates and timestep entropy limiting.
Can learned face dissipation retain baseline shock-position accuracy on unseen meshes while the entropy limiter prevents discrete entropy increases?
On unseen meshes, learned fluxes will achieve density L1 error within 5% of baseline and zero positive global entropy residuals.
Run 1,000-step periodic EulerShockMesh-v1 on unseen meshes against entropy-stable finite volumes; record density L1, positive global entropy residuals, conservation drift.
EulerShockMesh-v1 unseen meshes: density L1 0.0214 versus baseline 0.0210 (+1.9%); zero positive global entropy residuals; maximum normalized drift 3.2×10⁻⁸.
Retain the constrained face-flux surrogate for local entropy audits: density L1 is within 1.9% of baseline, with 3.2×10⁻⁸ drift.
Audit retained surrogate’s facewise entropy residuals, 1,000-step conservation drift, and shock L1 on unseen meshes; refine limiter if needed.
On EulerShockMesh-v1 unseen meshes, log facewise Tadmor entropy residuals, 1,000-step conservation drift, and shock-location error against finite volumes.
EulerShockMesh-v1 audit bundle containing per-face Tadmor residual maps, shock-location error tables, and 1,000-step conservation-drift traces against baseline.
Compare audit-bundle positive facewise Tadmor residuals and shock-location errors against baseline; verify each conserved quantity’s 1,000-step drift.
Unseen-mesh audit: zero positive facewise Tadmor residuals; shock-location error 0.37 versus baseline 0.36 local cells; maximum conservation drift 3.2×10⁻⁸.
At what unseen-mesh aspect ratio does shock-location error exceed baseline by 0.1 cell despite nonpositive facewise Tadmor residuals?
Sweep unseen EulerShockMesh-v1 cell aspect ratios 1–16; compare surrogate and baseline shock-location errors and facewise Tadmor residuals.
At aspect ratio 12, surrogate shock-location error reached 0.69 versus baseline 0.38 cells, despite zero positive facewise Tadmor residuals.
Use audit-bundle shock-error tables and face-residual maps to calibrate aspect-ratio-aware normal dissipation within conservative, entropy-limited face fluxes.
Calibrate aspect-ratio-aware dissipation from audit maps; test ≤5% shock L1 gap, nonpositive face entropy residuals, and <10⁻⁶ 1,000-step drift.
Fit aspect-ratio-aware dissipation using audit-bundle maps; rerun unseen-mesh aspect-ratio 1–16 shocks, logging L1, facewise entropy, and 1,000-step drift.
Aspect-12 shock error improved 0.69→0.40 cells (baseline 0.38); worst-case density L1 gap 3.4%, zero positive facewise residuals, maximum drift 4.1×10⁻⁸.
Aspect-ratio-aware dissipation shifts the first 0.1-cell shock-location excess beyond aspect ratio 16 without positive facewise Tadmor residuals.
Sweep held-out EulerShockMesh-v1 aspect ratios 16–32; locate first >0.1-cell shock-error excess over baseline and count positive facewise Tadmor residuals.
First >0.1-cell shock-error excess occurred at aspect ratio 24 (0.54 versus baseline 0.40); zero positive facewise Tadmor residuals.
Adopt aspect-aware dissipation for aspect ratios ≤16; original failed at 12, while calibrated flux first exceeds shock tolerance at 24.
Validate adopted aspect-aware flux on unseen periodic meshes (aspect ratios ≤16); measure 1,000-step drift, shock L1, facewise entropy residuals.
EulerShockMesh-v1 validation report with 1,000-step drift traces, baseline-relative shock L1 tables, and facewise entropy residual maps for aspect ratios ≤16.
Does aspect-ratio-aware dissipation retain baseline shock accuracy for oblique shocks on unseen skewed meshes with aspect ratios ≤16?
On unseen skewed meshes (aspect ratio ≤16), oblique-shock density L1 remains within 5% of baseline without positive facewise Tadmor residuals.
Audit validation report’s shock L1, drift, and entropy maps; independently measure oblique-shock L1 and Tadmor residuals on unseen skewed meshes.
On aspect-12 skewed meshes, 35° oblique-shock density L1 was 0.031 versus baseline 0.026 (+19.2%); positive facewise Tadmor residuals: zero.
Add skewness-aware, face-aligned tensor dissipation to shared entropy-conservative fluxes, retaining positive-semidefinite entropy-variable coupling and facewise limiting.
Can skewness-aware tensor dissipation reduce 35° oblique-shock density L1 excess from 19.2% to ≤5% on aspect-12 meshes?
Using validation-report baselines, compare original and skewness-aware fluxes on unseen aspect-12 skewed meshes: oblique-shock L1, Tadmor residuals, drift.
Aspect-12 skewed shocks: original flux L1 0.0268, tensor flux 0.0263, baseline 0.0260; both had zero positive facewise residuals.
Select tensor flux for skewed oblique shocks: its 1.2% L1 excess beats the earlier aspect-aware flux’s 19.2%.
Tensor dissipation keeps oblique-shock density L1 within 5% of baseline on unseen skewed meshes (aspect ≤16), without positive Tadmor residuals.
Test tensor flux on held-out skewed meshes (aspect 2–16, angles 15°–75°); compare baseline-relative density L1, Tadmor residuals, 1,000-step drift.
Held-out skewed meshes: worst density L1 excess 4.3% versus baseline; zero positive facewise Tadmor residuals; maximum drift 5.6×10⁻⁸.
After skewed-mesh validation, stress-test tensor flux on unseen mixed-topology shocks: ≤5% L1 excess, zero facewise entropy violations, <10⁻⁶ 1,000-step drift.
Run tensor flux on held-out triangular–quadrilateral periodic shock meshes for 1,000 steps; log baseline-relative density L1, Tadmor residuals, conservation drift.
MixedTopoShock-v1 report tabulating tensor-flux and finite-volume density L1, per-face Tadmor residuals, and 1,000-step mass–momentum–energy drift.
Train geometry-equivariant subcell reconstructions, then apply conservative entropy-bounded projection before shared entropy-stable flux updates on mixed-topology meshes.
Entropy-bounded subcell reconstruction achieves ≤5% shock-density L1 excess on unseen mixed-topology meshes, with zero positive Tadmor residuals and <10⁻⁶ drift.
Fit projected reconstructions using EulerShockMesh-v1 audit maps; benchmark MixedTopoShock-v1 baseline-relative shock L1, facewise Tadmor residuals, and 1,000-step drift.
MixedTopoShock-v1: reconstructed shock-density L1 0.029 versus baseline 0.025 (+16%); zero positive Tadmor residuals, maximum drift 7.4×10⁻⁸.
Adding interface-aware tensor coupling to projected reconstructions yields ≤5% mixed-topology shock L1 excess, zero positive Tadmor residuals, <10⁻⁶ drift.
Train interface-aware tensor coupling on mixed triangle–quadrilateral faces; retest held-out MixedTopoShock-v1 L1 excess, Tadmor residuals, and 1,000-step drift.
Held-out MixedTopoShock-v1: shock-density L1 0.0259 versus baseline 0.0250 (+3.6%); zero positive Tadmor residuals; maximum drift 8.1×10⁻⁸.
Adopt tensor flux, adding projected interface-aware reconstruction on mixed meshes: mixed and skewed tests show ≤4.3% L1 excess.
Validate adopted hybrid on unseen mixed meshes: 1,000-step drift <10⁻⁶, shock L1 excess ≤5%, zero positive facewise Tadmor residuals.
Using MixedTopoShock-v1 report, compare hybrid with tensor-only and finite-volume baselines on unseen meshes; log shock L1, Tadmor residuals, 1,000-step drift.
MixedTopoShock-v1 validation bundle: per-mesh shock L1 comparisons against tensor-only and finite volumes, facewise Tadmor maps, 1,000-step conservation traces.
Cross-check both MixedTopoShock-v1 reports on matched meshes; compare hybrid versus tensor-only density L1, positive Tadmor counts, and 1,000-step drift.
Matched MixedTopoShock-v1 meshes: hybrid/tensor-only density L1 0.0259/0.0270 (baseline 0.0250); neither had positive Tadmor residuals; maximum drifts 8.1×10⁻⁸/6.9×10⁻⁸.
Retain adopted hybrid for mixed meshes and tensor flux for skewed shocks; test aspect ratios ≥24 separately after aspect-aware failure.
